units: SI; levels in dB re 20 uPa (SPL) or 1 pW (sound power); angles in degrees

provenance_tags.MEASURED: published measurement or our analysis of a downloaded public-domain recording
provenance_tags.ROM: reduced-order model chosen here; physically motivated, not validated

telemetry._note: Fields each runtime must supply every audio control tick (>= 30 Hz). 'emission' fields are looked up at the EMISSION time t_e (see propagation), so keep >= 20 s of history.

phase.values: 0 PAD,1 S1_BURN,2 COAST_SEP,3 COAST_S2,4 S2_BURN,5 ORBIT,6 S2_DEPLETED

thrust.note: total thrust of the ACTIVE stage

mdot.note: total mass flow of the active stage

nozzle_pos.unreal: vehicle actor nozzle-exit world location (cm -> m)
nozzle_pos.python: ECI y[0:3] - pad, rotated into local ENU (render_launch.py)
nozzle_pos.note: active stage nozzle exit plane centre

plume_axis.unreal: -(body x axis) from the ascent quaternion
plume_axis.note: direction the EXHAUST flows (opposite the nose)

listener_pos.note: camera/listener position in the same frame

listener_pa.note: ambient pressure at the LISTENER (USSA-1976 at listener altitude)

events._note: names as emitted by sim.ts / AetherSim.cpp / sim.py
events.LIFTOFF: pad clamp release (pad layer keeps its height law)
events.SES: stage-2 start (vacuum engine: onboard structure only)

acoustic_efficiency.source: NASA SP-8072 s2.1.1: 0.2-1.0 % for most data, 0.5 % most probable, 1 % conservative

jet_velocity.formula: U = thrust / mdot  (effective exhaust velocity incl. pressure thrust)
jet_velocity.note: SP-8072 uses the fully expanded exit velocity; thrust/mdot is within ~3 % of it for this vehicle and is available identically in all three runtimes.

sound_power.throttle_and_engines: mdot and thrust already include throttle and engine count; W scales ~ throttle * U^2

source_continuum_cutoff.note: keeps W from being radiated into a near-vacuum; irrelevant below ~65 km where 1-stage noise IS heard on the ground (Mathews et al. 2020 measured the MECO level drop at 8.3 km)

spectrum.source: NASA SP-8072 Fig. 5, faired curve, digitised by eye (+-1.5 dB), renormalised to unit area
spectrum.definition: 10*log10( W(f) * U / (W * De) ) at St = f*De/U ; band power W_b = W * integral over band of 10^(level/10) dSt

under_expanded_diameter.formula: D_spec = max(De, sqrt(n) * Dj)  with Dj from plume ROM (physics/plume_rom.py)
under_expanded_diameter.note: lowers the spectrum as the plume balloons at altitude; not validated

reference_condition.note: stage 1, sea level, full thrust: f_peak = 0.02*U/De

check_falcon9.source: Mathews et al. 2020 (peak ~20 Hz at peak directivity, 8.3 km); Gee et al. 2023 Artemis-I mean 1/3-oct peak 20 Hz

core_length.formula: x_t = 3.45 * De * (1 + 0.38 * M_e)^2  (De = cluster-equivalent diameter, merged flow)
core_length.source: curve fit commonly used for SP-8072 Fig. 11 (core length vs exit Mach; the report gives the plot, not the formula - fit gives 19.5 De at M_e=3.63 (plume ROM, stage 1), inside the figure's rocket data band)
core_length.apparent_source_offset: x_src = 1.5 * x_t along the plume axis from the nozzle exit (SP-8072 Fig. 12: maxima at 1-2 core lengths)
core_length.M_e_source: plume ROM Me (physics/plume_rom.py) at the current throttle

directivity.source: SP-8072 Fig. 10 shapes (digitised), angle-warped so the implied OASPL peak (and 6-dB points) sit at the Falcon 9 measured 65 deg (45-80 deg) of Mathews et al. 2020/2021. Angle measured from the EXHAUST-FLOW direction.
directivity.usage: DI(f) = bilinear interp in (log St, angle) with St = f*De/U clamped to [0.004, 0.4]; add to band SPL

geometric_spreading.r_eff: sqrt(r^2 + r0^2), r0 = x_t (near-field limit: source extent ~ supersonic core length)
geometric_spreading.note: rho_L*c_L at the listener (intensity is conserved along the ray through the stratified atmosphere)

emission_time.formula: t_r = t_e + |x_src(t_e) - x_L| / c_path ; solve for t_e each tick (fixed-point, 3 iterations from last t_e)
emission_time.c_path: harmonic mean of USSA-1976 sound speed along the straight ray (wind ignored)
emission_time.doppler_policy: Doppler comes ONLY from reading the source at t_e (variable delay line / control-rate time warp of the source playback). Do NOT add a separate pitch shift. Broadband loops: playbackRate = dt_e/dt_r clamped to [0.5, 1.5].

atmospheric_absorption.model: ISO 9613-1:1993 pure-tone absorption, evaluated at band centre, integrated along the ray with local T, p, humidity

formula.h: molar concentration of water vapour in %: h = RH*(psat/pr)/(pa/pr), psat/pr = 10^(-6.8346*(273.16/T)^1.261 + 4.6151)

humidity_profile.note: constant-RH surface, water-vapour molar fraction decays exp(-z/2500 m)

crackle_band_policy.formula: A_crackle(f) = A_iso(f) - (A_iso(f) - A_iso(f_ref*(f/f_ref)^exponent)) * min(1, nonlinear_range_m / r)   for f > f_ref
crackle_band_policy.note: weak-shock theory: while the wave stays nonlinear, the shock's HF content is regenerated by steepening, so the crackle layer is absorbed as if each band f > f_ref were at f_ref*(f/f_ref)^exponent (jet_mix keeps full ISO 9613-1 per band). Beyond nonlinear_range_m (old-age region) normal absorption resumes for the remaining path fraction.

ground_reflection.formula: G = +6 dB for f < fc, +3 dB for f > 4*fc (log-interp between); fc = c/(4*dPath), dPath = 2*h_L*sin(psi)
ground_reflection.note: coherent pressure doubling at LF over hard ground, incoherent (+3 dB) at HF; avoids an audible comb filter. For listeners > 30 m above ground (aerial cameras) use G = +3 dB at LF only below 40 Hz.

terrain_shielding.note: Mathews et al. 2021 report terrain shielding effects; not modelled (flat ground).

crackle.weight: w_c = smoothstep((Mc - 1.5)/2.0) * clamp(pa/101325, 0, 1)^0.5 ; layer amplitude = clamp(w_c * reference_weight * w_dir(theta) * g_nl(r), 0, max_weight)
crackle.note: Crackle (shock content) needs supersonic convection of the large-scale structures (Ffowcs Williams et al. 1975; Petitjean et al. 2006) - always satisfied by rocket plumes, so w_c is driven mainly by ambient density (plume shear-layer intensity). See layer_gain_rule.
crackle.weight_rationale: ARTISTIC (listening feedback: wants loud banging/popping 'like a large bullet'). Raised from 0.5 / 4.0. The crackle asset was regenerated as sparse, strong, sharp-fronted shock events (see docs section 6); event timing stays non-periodic (inter-event CV ~1.5-2).

nonlinear_growth.formula: g_nl = 1 + max_gain * min(1, log2(1 + ln(max(r, x_t)/x_t)) / log2_saturation)
nonlinear_growth.note: Mathews et al. 2020 measured Falcon 9 SPL above the noise floor up to 10 kHz at 8.3 km and attribute it to nonlinear propagation; spherical-wave distortion grows ~ln(r/r0).

directivity.note: crackle is Mach-wave radiation, strongest around the peak-radiation angle and weak toward the plume axis (derivative skewness peaks near max directivity in Gee et al.'s rocket/jet measurements); peak taken from the Falcon 9 OASPL peak (65 deg)

crackle.layer_gain_rule: crackle amplitude w = clamp(w_c * reference_weight * w_dir * g_nl, 0, max_weight) (LINEAR) x the jet-group EQ gain, plus the crackle absorption policy (propagation.atmospheric_absorption.crackle_band_policy). The crackle asset is normalised so that at amplitude 1 it carries the same >400 Hz energy as the linear jet. reference_weight 0.5 (with exponent 0.2) was the value tuned to the measured dSk (pad 1-3, ~6 km 3-8); 1.5 is the ARTISTIC value after listening feedback, so crackle is now deliberately stronger than the recordings suggest. Play it sample-aligned with jet_mix when possible.
crackle.propagation_note: No nonlinear propagation SOLVER: distance growth of shock content is represented by g_nl and the reduced crackle absorption (both ROM). Real waveform steepening over km is NOT simulated.

deriv_skewness_shock_formation.source: Reichman et al. (cited in Gee et al. 2018 JASA 144, EL40): dSk~5 <-> significant shocks, needs fs >~ 100 f_peak

pad_interaction.weight: w_pad = exp(-max(h_nozzle, 0) / h_e),  h_e = 10 * De  (~31 m for stage 1)
pad_interaction.source_position: flame-trench exit: pad + trench_dir * 60 m at ground level (trench_dir = horizontal, away from the camera is fine if unknown)
pad_interaction.deflected_efficiency_note: SP-8072 Fig. 4: deflected exhausts radiate LESS total power (0.05-0.2 %), so the pad layer adds low-mid roar + water/steam texture while w_pad also lowers the free-jet term: jet term x (1 - 0.5*w_pad)

ignition_overpressure.source: Mathews et al. 2020: IOP waveform period ~0.8 s, spectral peaks ~3 and 16 Hz at 8.3 km (Falcon 9). Casiano 2009 (NTRS 20090032104): IOP from rapid exhaust acceleration during engine start.
ignition_overpressure.asset: ignition_overpressure (separate one-shot, emitted offset_s after IGNITION at the trench exit)
ignition_overpressure.level_rule: scalar gain: G_dB = oa(D_jet_liftoff) + level_db_re_full_thrust_jet - rms_main_dbfs (asset's RMS over its main 0.5 s), D_jet_liftoff = the jet group's digital target at a full-thrust liftoff state for this listener; cabin: minus the mass-law TL per band
ignition_overpressure.level_rationale: ARTISTIC (listening feedback): +6 dB over the full-thrust jet so the ignition overpressure reads as a clear low thump. Shape: Friedlander-type compression (2 ms rise, ~0.12 s positive phase) low-passed at 180 Hz + the measured ~0.8 s period and 16 Hz component (MEASURED, Mathews 2020) + three pad/terrain reflections (ARTISTIC).
ignition_overpressure.directivity: strongest along the flame-trench exit (Gee et al. 2023 Artemis-I)

airborne_plume_reaches_vehicle.note: once the vehicle outruns its own exhaust noise (M > ~1) plume sound cannot propagate upstream to the forward vehicle; liftoff reflection from the pad is the dominant external load

structure_borne.formula: L_struct = 20*log10(thrust / thrust_ref_stage1) + struct_ref_db ; continues in vacuum
structure_borne.spectrum_source: shape of NASA GSFC-STD-7000 (GEVS) random-vibration qualification spectrum (20-2000 Hz), plus damped structural modes - SHAPE ONLY, no level claim

digital_reference_levels_dbfs.note: RMS dBFS; structure scales 20*log10(thrust/thrust_ref), aero 20*log10(w_aero); cabin aero also gets 0.5 x mass-law TL as spectral tilt

aero_buffet.source: same law Aether already uses for camera shake (frontend/src/engine/Effects.ts)

onboard.vacuum_cutoff: external airborne gain = 0 when listener pa < 1 Pa (and continuously via the rho*c factor above that)

level_mapping.note: Real launch levels span >80 dB across viewpoints; a microphone engineer sets gain per position. Each listener preset has a fixed mic gain chosen from its predicted maximum SPL; levels then follow physics with an optional loudness compression k (1 = physical, 0.5 recommended for games).
level_mapping.dbfs: RMS dBFS = target_peak_dbfs + k * (Lp - Lp_max_preset)  (target_peak_dbfs is the RMS level at the loudest moment)
level_mapping.rationale: ARTISTIC (2026-10-19 listening feedback: 'quite quiet'). -9 dBFS RMS at the loudest moment leaves ~8 dB for crest; crackle bangs and the IOP thump are allowed to hit the limiter (that is the intended 'large bullet' punch). Previous values: -18 dBFS, k_game 0.6.

limiter.type: look-ahead peak limiter (feed-forward, brick-wall at the ceiling)
recipe: 1. required gain reduction GRreq[n] = max(0, 20*log10(|x[n]|) - ceiling_dbfs)  (dB, >= 0)
2. look-ahead hold: GRh[n] = max(GRreq[n .. n+L]),  L = round(lookahead_ms * fs / 1000)
3. release: GRr[n] = max(GRh[n], GRr[n-1] * exp(-1 / (release_ms * fs / 1000)))  (exponential recovery of the dB reduction)
4. attack smoothing: GR[n] = mean(GRr[n-L+1 .. n])  (linear ramp over the look-ahead; never below GRreq at the peak)
5. y[n] = x[n] * 10^(-GR[n]/20); real time: compute GR on the input and apply it to the input delayed by L samples
6. safety: clip |y| to the ceiling (a no-op except for float rounding)
limiter.browser_realisation: DynamicsCompressorNode (spec look-ahead ~6 ms) threshold -1 dB, knee 0, ratio 20, attack 5 ms, release 150 ms, followed by a static clip at the ceiling (the node's automatic makeup gain, about +0.6 dB at these settings, is absorbed by that clip)

anti_repetition.formula: out(t) = cos(phi)*loop(p) + sin(phi)*loop(p + 0.618*N),  phi = pi/4 + pi/4*sin(2*pi*t/37.3)
anti_repetition.note: Each loop plays as two voices (golden-ratio offset) with an equal-power crossfade on an incommensurate period, so the 24 s loop pattern does not audibly repeat. Use the SAME p and phi for rumble_lf, jet_mix and crackle (sync group 'jet'). Different groups may use different start offsets (e.g. aero +7.3 s).

policy: warp <= 1 (incl. slow motion): control parameters and propagation delays in SIM time; layer playback stays at real-time rate (no pitch change); one-shots play at normal speed.
1 < warp <= 4: parameters in sim time, delays shrink in wall-clock (consistent ordering); suppress one-shots that would overlap; airborne gain -6 dB*log2(warp)/2.
warp > 4: fade airborne to -24 dB over 1 s and keep only rumble_lf + onboard_structure (time-lapse ambience).

listeners._note: positions relative to the pad, metres, local ENU (x east = downrange, y north, z up). Aether render-world uses y-up: map (east, north, up) -> render (x, -z, y) as CameraRig does.

Pad.notes: 405 m: near field, pad layer + crackle dominate first 8 s

Engines.notes: rides with the vehicle 26 m off the engines: no delay change, no Doppler; airborne plume level from source model with r = 30 m, theta = 100 deg; fades with w_air like onboard

Onboard.notes: structure_borne + w_air plume + aero_buffet; no external sound in vacuum

Aerial.notes: helicopter 650 m up: ground G per note

Free.notes: treat as chase at the user distance; vacuum rule applies above ~80 km

Orbital.notes: silent externally; optional onboard_structure at -20 dB if the camera is attached

outside_observer.notes: any distance: full model; 5 km and 20 km presets validated in docs

cabin_passenger.notes: onboard + cabin_transmission_loss on the airborne part; structure_borne dominant

chase_camera.notes: as Aether 'Engines' with r = camera distance; cap Lp at preset max

vacuum.notes: external = 0; cabin passenger still hears structure_borne while engines burn

layers.name: rumble_lf
layers.role: LF exhaust rumble, slow irregular modulation (0.08-3 Hz)

layers.name: jet_mix
layers.role: turbulent jet-mixing noise, main broadband body

layers.name: crackle
layers.role: shock HF of the steepened <2 kHz (energetic) jet waveform; amplitude = w (see profile crackle.layer_gain_rule) x jet EQ

oneshots.name: ignition
oneshots.role: igniter tick and staggered engine light-ups

oneshots.name: ignition_overpressure
oneshots.tag: MEASURED period/16 Hz + ARTISTIC shape and level
oneshots.role: ignition overpressure: low thump (front at 0.1 s into the file); scalar gain per pad_interaction.ignition_overpressure.level_rule

oneshots.name: meco_tail
oneshots.role: thrust tail-off: spectrum slides down with chamber pressure + plume-collapse rumble

asset_calibration.note: rumble_lf, jet_mix and crackle share ONE gain (their relative levels are physical): rumble_lf+jet_mix power sum = -18 dBFS RMS (lower if a crackle peak would exceed -1 dBFS; see jet_group_rms_dbfs) and represents the SP-8072 source spectrum at the reference condition (stage 1, sea level, full thrust, U=2786 m/s, De=3.096 m, f_peak=18 Hz, peak-directivity, no absorption). Other loops are normalised to -20 dBFS RMS; their absolute level comes from the mapping formulas.
asset_calibration.runtime_eq_rule: EQ_dB[b] = D[b] - A_group[b]; D = digital target band level from the model, A_group = the group's asset band level (layers[].octave_db power-summed over the group)

imap_blast1_startup_rise_db_per_s.note: Blast-1: -65 -> -20 dBFS before clipping; rise time of the engine-start ramp at a near-pad mic
